answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using bonded collateral stakes that form a defensive reef around the network. Each node must lock capital to broadcast a valid coordination signal, using cryptographic commitments as the structural timber of its identity. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locked capital reserves and slashed deposits per forged node. However, this mechanism disenfranchises low-resource agents and traps liquidity in unproductive escrow.
